sourceInformation.genre: Arcade sports (cricket), over the top, with a comedy story campaign
sourceInformation.perspective: 2.5D in projected-3D views: a TV broadcast camera behind the bowler for every delivery, a high wide camera following the ball, close-ups and a side-on review camera; story scenes in a three-quarter view
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge v0.85.2 (the full engine, modified), AI Hub session client 1.4.0, plain JavaScript, Web Audio; tests on Node and Playwright 1.63.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: The engine's HD Humanoid pixel style at 320x240 expanded, canvas lighting, engine shapes and materials, with new cricket assets (stumps, sight screens, the pub, the Thrumptonator, Doris the cow and more)
sourceInformation.animation: The engine's procedural Humanoid rigs, with a cricket layer of IK post-poses: two-handed bat swings by shot family, the bowler's overarm windmill, umpire signals; E.move throws, poses and dives
sourceInformation.audio: Chip-synth music in layers (base, drums, fire), synthesized effects, a crowd engine (bed, applause, roars) and Animalese-style gibberish formant voices, all in code
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1: a parallel Super Over at the Megadome for 1 to 4 players, with the game's own card
sourceInformation.testing: Headless engine (game.advance, game.debug), scripted playthroughs and bot matches behind one command, Playwright browser checks, the AI Hub harness
sourceInformation.research: None beyond the plan, the engine handoff docs and kits, and the AI Hub protocol README and example
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux; browser unknown

testingFeedback: About 41 issues: 25 gameplay or logic bugs, 7 visual or layout problems, 6 balance problems (wides, a passive CPU batter, a slow sandy outfield) and a few test-harness mistakes of my own.

8 were game breaking: a dead ball that never ended (a review timer below zero), two scenes that could only finish once (stale flags), a misnamed dead-ball handler, the camera pointed thousands of units away (radians read as degrees), an engine floor-bake crash at the low broadcast pitch, long throws counted as overthrows (15-second balls), and a commentary crash in CPU-only matches.
The forced-outcome scenarios (sim-field, sim-arcade, attract): they drive the real delivery director end to end, and found most of the logic bugs and all the stuck-ball ones.
The solved-delivery accuracy check: it mostly measured the 1/120 s step quantization of the pitching point, not a game bug.
engineFeedback: The Humanoid rig: a dressed, lit, animated cricketer from one options object, and solvePose open to wrapping, so bat swings and a bowling windmill could be added by IK.
Yes: a custom View keeps its pitch in radians (pitchDeg holds the degrees), which put the camera thousands of units away; and a long press on a click kept clicked() null in a headless test.
Cricket itself: the ball physics and predictor, the delivery director, fielding and running, the umpiring and reviews, plus the forced-outcome layer the attract mode and dev mode share.
Framing a strongly foreshortened broadcast camera: the chunked floor bake broke at a low pitch, and the far end needed a painted panorama.

A cricket bat weapon, batting pads, moustaches/beards/glasses, PlayStation glyphs by default with Xbox as the option, Create + Options left to the hub, ten cached floor bakes, and a fix for the chunked floor cache trim.
A perspective (telephoto) camera option for ground views, so a TV-style sports camera needs no painted far-end panorama.
promptFeedback: The clear, testable definition of done, and the freedom to change the engine.
How much of a very large plan is binding when TASK.md says it wins on disagreement, and what "follow" means for the plan versus the AI Hub protocol.
Fitting a full cricket simulation, five grounds, a story, local and online multiplayer, an attract mode and a dev mode into one session with honest testing.
Give a target scope (minutes of play, number of modes) and say which plan features are required versus optional.

aiHub.name: Cricket Kerfuffle
aiHub.description: Smash sixes through the pub window, bowl flaming yorkers and save the village green from Lord Thrumpton across five outrageous grounds. Up to four players on one screen, or a Super Over showdown in AI Hub sessions.
aiHub.controls: Stick/WASD/mouse aim · Cross/J/click hit · Square/K/right-click loft · Circle/L defend · R1/Space run
